Descriptive statistics and intraclass correlations of model variables

Source: R/descriptives.R
descriptives.Rd

descriptives() summarizes the characteristics of variables used in latent profile and class analyses. It supports inspection of variability, observed ranges, and missingness before model estimation, as well as descriptive comparisons across groups.

For numeric variables, the function reports measures of central tendency and dispersion. When a grouping identifier is supplied, it also estimates intraclass correlations to describe clustering within groups. Summaries can be calculated for the full dataset or separately by an observed grouping variable. For supported fitted models, variables can also be summarized by assigned profile or group class.

Usage

descriptives(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
descriptives(x, vars = NULL, id = NULL, by = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A data frame, or a profile, class or transition fit (from lpa(), lca(), multilpa(), multilca(), or lta() with time-homogeneous transitions), whose own vars and id are then used. A single-level fit has no groups, so its table has no n_groups or icc. Anything else, including a fit of another family, raises latents_not_a_fit; describe the data frame it was fitted to instead.

...

Not used. For a data frame, any further argument raises a latents_unused_argument warning; for a fit, it raises latents_bad_argument.

vars

Character vector of column names to describe; repeated names are described once. Columns must be vectors: matrix-valued columns raise latents_bad_data. For a data frame, defaults to every numeric column other than id and by.

id

Optional. The column identifying the groups the rows are nested in. Supplying it adds n_groups and icc.

by

Optional. On a fitted model, "profile" or "group_class"; on a data frame, a column name. Each variable is then described once per level of it. Rows whose stratifier is NA form their own stratum, labelled NA and reported last, so every input row is counted in exactly one stratum.

Value

A base data.frame, one row per variable (or per variable and by level), with the columns

variable

character: the column described.

n

integer: observations with a value.

n_missing

integer: observations without one.

mean,sd,min,max

numeric; NA_real_ for a variable that is not numeric.

n_distinct

integer: distinct observed values.

n_groups,icc

present only when id is known. icc is the one-way random-effects estimate. It can be negative when the between-group mean square is smaller than the within-group mean square; this does not represent a negative population variance. Rows with a missing group identifier contribute to neither statistic.

With by, a first column named after the stratifier holds each stratum's value (NA for the stratum of missing values). For every variable, n + n_missing summed over the strata equals the number of input rows. When describing a fit by "profile" or "group_class", the model's assignment is used as the stratifier without replacing an indicator of the same name. A by named like one of the summary's own columns raises latents_bad_data. Describing no variables raises latents_nothing_to_describe.

Details

Summaries by fitted class use assigned membership and do not incorporate classification uncertainty. They describe the observations assigned to each class and should be distinguished from the model's estimated class-specific parameters. Rows excluded from classification are retained in a separate stratum with a missing class label, following the fit's drop_empty setting.

An intraclass correlation (ICC) near zero indicates little between-group variation in that variable's mean. It does not rule out group classes that differ in other variables, in profile prevalence, or in other features of the distributions.

References

Bliese, P. D. (2000). Within-group agreement, non-independence, and reliability. In K. J. Klein & S. W. J. Kozlowski (Eds.), Multilevel theory, research, and methods in organizations.

See also

multilpa() for model estimation and diagnostics() for diagnostics of a fitted model.

Examples

descriptives(
  course_engagement,
  vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
  id = "student"
)
#>     variable    n n_missing          mean        sd   min  max n_distinct
#> 1     browse 1422         0 -2.812940e-05 0.9890804 -3.14 2.49        398
#> 2   lectures 1422         0 -4.219409e-05 0.9889178 -2.91 3.22        399
#> 3 forum_read 1422         0  7.032349e-05 0.9890236 -2.73 2.81        400
#> 4 forum_post 1422         0 -2.109705e-05 0.9890038 -2.61 3.10        397
#> 5 attendance 1422         0  7.735584e-05 0.9889426 -2.45 2.41        401
#>   n_groups        icc
#> 1      106 0.19229259
#> 2      106 0.08779169
#> 3      106 0.22403384
#> 4      106 0.15034618
#> 5      106 0.22145308

# Missing stratification values form a separate stratum.
descriptives(data.frame(cohort = c("A", "A", "B", NA), score = 1:4),
             vars = "score", by = "cohort")
#>   cohort variable n n_missing mean        sd min max n_distinct
#> 1      A    score 2         0  1.5 0.7071068   1   2          2
#> 2      B    score 1         0  3.0        NA   3   3          1
#> 3   <NA>    score 1         0  4.0        NA   4   4          1

fit <- multilpa(
  course_engagement,
  vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
  id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,
  seed = 1
)
descriptives(fit)
#>     variable    n n_missing          mean        sd   min  max n_distinct
#> 1     browse 1422         0 -2.812940e-05 0.9890804 -3.14 2.49        398
#> 2   lectures 1422         0 -4.219409e-05 0.9889178 -2.91 3.22        399
#> 3 forum_read 1422         0  7.032349e-05 0.9890236 -2.73 2.81        400
#> 4 forum_post 1422         0 -2.109705e-05 0.9890038 -2.61 3.10        397
#> 5 attendance 1422         0  7.735584e-05 0.9889426 -2.45 2.41        401
#>   n_groups        icc
#> 1      106 0.19229259
#> 2      106 0.08779169
#> 3      106 0.22403384
#> 4      106 0.15034618
#> 5      106 0.22145308
descriptives(fit, by = "profile")
#>    profile   variable   n n_missing       mean        sd   min  max n_distinct
#> 1        1     browse 836         0  0.5422249 0.7644929 -2.31 2.49        285

#> 7        2   lectures 586         0 -0.6106655 0.7339385 -2.91 1.43        250

#> 10       2 attendance 586         0 -0.9239249 0.6108514 -2.45 0.83        230
#>    n_groups           icc
